subject: Random walk on only part of domain?

messages.author: 8c6b85a01a12e3e2
messages.subject: Random walk on only part of domain?
parts:
Hi,

I would like to know if it's possible to apply a random effect to only part of the domain.  

The specific context is I have a timeseries.  Until day 51, I want to assume it's entirely explained by a fixed effect. After day 50, I want to continue to model the fixed effect, but add in an RW2 to quantify a structurally-changing residual.  

Ideally I would just do something like define a column in the data that is all zeros through day 50 and then one from day 51 forward, and somehow multiply that by the rw2 effect. I realize this isn't quite right, but I hope my use case is clear. 

Any thoughts on how to do it?

Thanks,

--Mike

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random walk on only part of domain?
parts:
Hi,
I can think of a few options, but the simplest is probably this:

Let the initial value of a rw2 model define the pre-day-50 effect.
If Day is the day index variable, starting at 1, define
  ShiftedDay = pmax(1, Day - 49)
and use that in a rw2 effect, and don't use an intercept:,
 ~ f(ShiftedDay, model = "rw2", constr = FALSE) - 1
(or constr=TRUE and include an intercept, but I suspect that might be less easy to interpret in your case)

When looked at as a function of the original Day variable, this model has the behaviour you described.
In case you want a smooth transition , with a derivative = 0 condition at Day==50, that can be accomplished by adding a constraint on the difference between day 49 and 50:
Shift one day less than before:
  ShiftedDay = pmax(1, Day - 48)
formula:
 ~ f(ShiftedDay, model = "rw2", constr = FALSE, extraconstr=list(A=matrix(rep(c(-1,1,0),c(1,1,N-2)), e=0) - 1
where
  N = max(ShiftedDay)

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Random walk on only part of domain?
parts:
gGreat!

Yes, to constrain the start to zero, just add another constraint:
extraconstr = list(A = rbind(rep(c(-1,1,0),c(1,1,N-2), rep(c(1,0),c(1,N-1))), e = rbind(0, 0))

The constraint works by constraining A x = e, where x is the vector of values of the latent model component, so the above constraints are
-x[1]+x[2] = 0
x[1]  = 0
to get derivative zero and value zero at the start.

In this particular case, this can in principle be replaced by
x[1] = 0
x[2]  = 0
but personally I like the value&derivative version better for interpretability.

But yeah, such amazing support. Love it!  The solution works.

One more question after seeing results, is there a way to constrain to start at 0 too, not just slope, but value?   Not essential but something I want to explore.

Thanks again,

--Mike
